assertions.name: map_and_formula_gate
assertions.source: sigma1 sigma2^-1 maps to RL and Phi(RL) agrees between the Dedekind-sum formula and the RL-word count

assertions.name: three_methods_agree
assertions.source: Dedekind-sum Phi == RL-word count == n*Phi(RL) for both knots

description: Bean qou-rdmr: tests whether the Rademacher symbol of the canonical 3-braid word supplies theta_K. Both corpus knots are (sigma1 sigma2^-1)^n closures (4_1 n=2, Borromean n=3) mapping to (RL)^n in SL(2,Z); an RL-balanced word has Rademacher Phi = 0, confirmed by the Dedekind-sum formula, the RL-word count, and homogeneity. Phi vanishes for BOTH knots, so it predicts theta = 0 against targets 0.0589/0.2032 and cannot distinguish the anchors. Scope-(a) refutation of the symbol as the theta source; the Ghys word->winding programme is NOT refuted. Method discipline: predicts from the braid word alone, then compares; the T4 theta values are A_omega-conditioned and were never fitted to.

data.method_note: the gate earned its keep: the first run had sigma2^-1 bound to L^-1 rather than L (i.e. to sigma2), which sent sigma1 sigma2^-1 to ((0,1),(-1,1)) instead of RL and produced a spurious Phi = -2 for 4_1 that the RL-count and homogeneity cross-checks contradicted. A single-method computation would have reported that -2 as a signal.
data.no_fit_note: T4 theta values are A_omega-conditioned (circularity note); used for comparison only, never as a fit target
data.verdict: SCOPE-(a) REFUTATION of the naive Rademacher route. Both canonical words are (σ₁σ₂⁻¹)ⁿ — 4₁ at n=2, Borromean at n=3 — whose SL(2,ℤ) image is (RL)ⁿ. An RL-balanced word has Rademacher Φ = n − n = 0, confirmed three independent ways (Dedekind-sum formula, RL-word count, and homogeneity Φ(Aⁿ)=n·Φ(RL) with Φ(RL)=0). So Φ VANISHES for both knots: it predicts ϑ = 0 where the targets are 0.0589 and 0.2032, and it cannot even DISTINGUISH the two anchors, which is the minimum any word→ϑ map must do. The braid word does carry independent information (the binary precondition passed: the two anchors are two different words), but the Rademacher symbol is not the functional that extracts it — it is blind to the (RL)ⁿ family by construction. SCOPE: this refutes the symbol as the ϑ source, NOT the Ghys word→winding programme; a different quasimorphism (or the full linking datum rather than its Rademacher shadow) is not excluded. Nothing fitted; the T4 values were used for comparison only and are themselves A_ω-conditioned.
